newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat to new lows on fungus talk, EU subsidy.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat to new lows on fungus talk, EU subsidy.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures were lower at midsession and new contract lows were set with resurfacing fears about the karnal bunt fungus plus a hike by the European Union in its wheat export subsidy pressuring prices, traders said.
"The fungus talk in wheat is pressuring it," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
A spokesman for the Tennessee Department of Agriculture Thursday said karnal bunt fungus was found in winter wheat grown in one Tennessee county and is suspected in six other counties.

Tennessee isn't a large wheat producer but traders said the market continued to get hammered by reports of wheat exports being rejected due to karnal bunt, TCK smut and on fears of vomitoxin in U.S. wheat supplies.
The European Union Thursday increased to 19 ECUS its subsidy for wheat exports form last week's 13 ECUS.

The new contract low for March wheat was $3.68-1/2 a bushel as of 1140 CST, below the previous low of $3.74 set Wednesday. At 1140 CST, wheat was three to eight cents lower, with December down eight at $3.73. March was 5-1/2 lower at $3.69-1/2.
Nearby December remained at 16-month lows and touched a session low of $3.73 a bushel, the lowest level for a nearby contract since $3.68 was reached June 16, 1995.
Technical traders said the market remains in a bearish slide with key moving averages pointing to further downward moves.
Technical support in the December contract was broken at $3.79 and again at $3.73.

Short term indicators show the market as oversold with the nine day relative strength index for December at 19 points as of 1150 CST. Traders generally consider a market as oversold at an RSI of 30 or less.
The volume of selling in wheat was not heavy, mainly half million to three-quarter million bushel sell orders and scattered among several funds and commission houses, traders said.
Term Commodities, the marketing arm of Louis Dreyfus Corp was the chief buyer of one million bushels of December, traders said.
